post_message: “There is no need for the vaccine because hunger will kill my child before any vaccine-preventable disease does.”  Sabin's Boost Community is made up of immunization professionals in all parts of the world. For member Fri Delphine Chifor, who works in parts of Cameroon where conflict has stripped families of safety, income, and access to basic services, vaccines remain one of the few consistent shields children still have. But getting vaccinated can often seem like a secondary concern as parents grapple with urgent questions of where they will sleep tonight or how they will find their next meal.  Chifor shares how  the Cameroon Baptist Convention Health Services Immunization Program started intentionally shifting the way they engaged with families, addressing what mattered most to them first and offering essential vaccines at the same time.   The impact was immediate — not only did they vaccinate more than 163,000 children in less than a year, but they also screened thousands for malnutrition, gave away mosquito nets and medications, and provided more than 13,000 caregivers with nutrition and vaccine education.  Read the full story at the link in our bio.

post_message: English physician Dr. Edward Jenner is credited with creating the first vaccination. In 1796, he used material from cowpox (a disease related to smallpox) to inoculate 8-year-old James Phipps. Two months later, Jenner exposed Phipps to smallpox, but the child did not get the disease.  Vaccines have now saved an estimated 154 million lives — that's the equivalent of six lives every minute for the past 50 years — and the vast majority of lives saved were infants. Today, childhood vaccinations prevent an estimated 4 million deaths annually.  Learn more about the history and impact of vaccines, and how they work at the link in our bio.

post_message: The largest measles outbreak in the U.S. since 1991 has ended. Over the last six months, nearly 1,000 people — most of them unvaccinated children — were infected with the disease, and at least 21 were hospitalized with complications.  The South Carolina outbreak was focused in a county where the majority of schools had measles vaccination rates below the 95% threshold required to prevent outbreaks, and officials say the outbreak was stopped, in part, because of an uptick in getting the vaccine.  Measles can be fatal, can leave children more vulnerable to new infections for years, and can also cause dangerous, long-lasting complications, some of which may not develop until nearly a decade after infection.   See our infographic on measles below, and read more on how the South Carolina outbreak was brought under control in a story by NPR ⤵️ https://ow.ly/wPQj50YRc93

post_message: Dr. Sue Ann Costa Clemens has worked as a pediatrician in low- and middle-income countries where limited access to care generates overwhelming demand. She has worked as a vaccinologist, contributing to the development of more than 20 vaccines. And now, she is taking on what she describes as her “legacy work" — training the next generation of vaccinologists through programs at the University of Oxford and the University of Siena, where she launched the first master’s degree in vaccinology.   In a recent episode of our web series, Getting to Zero, she spoke with us about her journey in the field, and gave insight into the skills next-gen vaccinologists need to have. post_message: The hexavalent vaccine offers clear advantages over the pentavalent — fewer injections, simplified schedules, logistical efficiencies, and stronger integration of polio vaccination into routine services.   But the switch to hexavalent requires coordinated action across policy, financing, supply chains, service delivery, data systems, workforce capacity, communication, and vaccine safety surveillance.  To support countries navigating this complexity, the Hexavalent Vaccine Switch Early Adopters Workshop, convened in Dakar, Senegal in November 2025 by Sabin and Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, brought together national immunization leaders, Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG) members, regional partners, and global technical agencies from ten African countries at different stages of readiness.  To get an inside look at the insights from this meeting, see the resources guide: ⤵️ https://lnkd.in/eqFFsKSE
